subject: FYI: Off-record feedback from dinner with Henrik (BU 4)
body:
Sven,

Quick heads-up from tonight's dinner with the BU 4 leadership team in Helsinki. Henrik Andersson pulled me aside after the formal session and shared some concerns he didn't want to raise in the steering committee setting.

He's worried about the post-acquisition integration cost assumptions in the Aurora diligence model—specifically the IT systems harmonization budget. He thinks we're underestimating by 30-40% based on BU 4's experience with the 2024 ERP rollout. He mentioned their actual integration costs ran SEK 18M vs. the SEK 12M budget, and the Finnish target's legacy systems look similar in complexity.

He was clear this is off-the-record and didn't want to be seen as blocking the deal in front of the other GMs, but he wanted someone on the strategy side to know before the board readout. He's concerned the board will approve based on incomplete cost visibility.

Thought you should have this before Thursday's presentation. Let me know if you want to discuss.

Best,
Johan

---
Johan Nyström
Partner, Nordic M&A Advisory
Bergman & Partners
Mobile: +46 70 234 5678

subject: TransLog Sverige preliminary materials - requested by 2026-01-28
body:
Sven,

Attached are the preliminary materials on TransLog Sverige you requested for the logistics sector strategic options review.

Key highlights:
- Revenue ~SEK 890M (2025), EBITDA margin 11.2%
- Family-owned, founder (age 67) exploring succession options
- Strong regional presence in Västra Götaland, limited national footprint
- Complementary to BU 7's existing logistics assets

Two points need your attention before Tuesday's call:

1. Their CFO mentioned informally that a PE fund (Nordic Capital) made an indicative approach in December. No exclusivity, but creates timeline pressure if we're interested.

2. Valuation expectation appears anchored at 9-10x EBITDA. Our internal model (assuming 15% synergy capture) supports max 7.5x. Bridging this gap will require either better synergy quantification or a phased earnout structure.

I can join Tuesday's strategy review call if helpful to discuss positioning, or we can keep this off-record until you've socialized internally.

Let me know if you need the full financial model before the weekend.

Best,
Johan

subject: Finnish Competition Authority filing - draft submission for review
body:
Sven,

Attached is the draft notification for the Finnish Competition Authority (Kilpailu- ja kuluttajavirasto) for Project Aurora.

Critical timeline:
- Submission deadline: 2026-02-09 (14 calendar days from signing)
- Authority review period: typically 30 days, but can extend to 4 months if Phase II triggered
- Our assessment: low risk of Phase II given market share thresholds

Three items require Vasaholm input by Monday 2026-01-27 COB:

1. **Market share data**: We need confirmed 2025 revenue figures for BU 3 and BU 7 in the 'precision components for industrial automation' segment. The target's 8.2% Finnish market share is solid, but we're missing Vasaholm's current position.

2. **Customer overlap analysis**: Preliminary review shows 4 shared customers (Kone, Wärtsilä, Valmet, Metso). Please confirm whether any have exclusivity or preferred-supplier arrangements that could raise vertical integration concerns.

3. **Divestiture scenario**: Low probability, but if the Authority requires a remedy, would Vasaholm consider divesting the target's Tampere facility (22% of target revenue) to preserve the deal? This is contingency planning only.

Karin Bergström at Linklaters has the commercial context. I'll coordinate with her on items 1-2, but item 3 is a board-level decision—flag to CEO/CFO if needed.

Please confirm receipt and timeline for Vasaholm inputs.

Best regards,
Mika Virtanen
Senior Associate, Competition Law
Lakitoimisto Virtanen Oy
+358 40 123 4567

subject: IndustriWatch Weekly: Volvo Group restructuring, Nordic M&A pipeline update
body:
INDUSTRIWATCH WEEKLY | January 26, 2026

=== TOP STORIES ===

• Volvo Group announces major restructuring: splitting truck and construction equipment divisions into separate legal entities by Q3 2026. Analyst consensus: unlock ~15% shareholder value.

• Nordic M&A pipeline: 18 industrial deals in diligence phase (total disclosed value SEK 12.4B). Strongest activity in automation/robotics and green energy sectors.

• Swedish krona strengthens to 10.85 SEK/EUR on Riksbank rate hold signal.

=== SECTOR DEEP DIVE: Logistics & Distribution ===

Private equity interest in Nordic logistics assets continues to accelerate. Three notable transactions in Q4 2025:
- Nordic Capital acquired DanLog (Denmark) for ~8.5x EBITDA
- EQT exploring options for Norwegian freight consolidator NorCargo
- Family-owned Swedish players (revenue <SEK 1B) receiving unsolicited approaches

Industry sources report valuation compression for sub-scale regional players without digital capabilities. Premium multiples (9-11x) reserved for assets with national coverage or tech-enabled offerings.

=== COMPLIANCE WATCH ===

EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reporting requirements take effect March 2026...
